question: Earlier studies suggested muscle could use only about 20 g of protein per meal. A 2023 trial gave 100 g. What happened?
options: The extra was burnt as fuel
The excess was stored as fat
answer: Muscle built more, for longer. After whole-body resistance exercise, 100 g of milk protein raised muscle protein building more than 25 g did, and kept it raised through all 12 hours measured. Earlier trials had used smaller doses and watched for only a few hours, so a slower, longer response looked like a ceiling.
move: A limit found by looking briefly may only be a limit of the looking.
trap: Holding to the familiar 20 g ceiling and expecting the rest wasted.
source: Trommelen et al., Cell Reports Medicine, 2023
reference: Trommelen et al., The anabolic response to protein ingestion during recovery from exercise has no upper limit in magnitude and duration in vivo in humans, Cell Reports Medicine, 2023
